storm.summary_layperson: No thunderstorms anywhere near the cove tonight, but a Wind Advisory is active for gusty north winds — expect a blustery evening rather than a stormy one.
storm.local_effect_blurb: Air–water gap is inverted (air already ~2°F cooler than the 68°F Sound at 4 PM, widening to almost 8°F by 8 PM) — no marine-layer buffer tonight, though it's moot with nothing on radar to buffer against.
storm.detail_html:
Radar (KOKX) shows no storm cells anywhere near the cove this afternoon, and HRRR model CAPE sits at 0 J/kg through the entire forecast window — there is no instability in the atmosphere for thunderstorms to build on, despite an active regional Wind Advisory.

That advisory (issued by NWS Upton, in effect from 2:48 PM today through Sunday 6 AM) is a synoptic wind event — a broad north/northeast flow bringing sustained wind near 20 mph and gusts as high as 32 mph — not a thunderstorm signal. It's why the wind-side forecast below is up, but it carries no lightning or convective risk.

The Sound's usual protective marine layer isn't in play tonight: water (67.8°F) is already running warmer than the air even at 4 PM, and that gap only grows as the air keeps cooling into the evening — the opposite of the setup needed to stabilize the boundary layer and choke incoming storms. It's moot for this window regardless, since there is nothing on radar to buffer against.

Bottom line for the cove: no thunderstorm risk through 10 PM. Expect a windy, north-breezy evening rather than a stormy one — the sky risk tonight is essentially the same in Riverside as anywhere else in the region.

What would change the call: any new convective initiation showing up on KOKX radar, or CAPE building above the 1500 J/kg threshold in a later HRRR cycle. Neither is indicated tonight.

wind.regime_label: Moderate gradient wind — no sea breeze in play

hourly.shift_note: steady, holding NNE (beyond HRRR range — extrapolated)

wind.tactics_blurb: Moderate-to-strong N/NNE gradient wind, no sea breeze in play — a Wind Advisory is active for gusts near 25–28 kt. Wind holds steady in direction and speed straight through the window since it's not solar-driven. Stay center, no strong shift bias expected, but rig for the gusts.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
Today fails the two-ingredient sea-breeze test outright: inland air is running about 2°F cooler than the Sound (air–water differential of -1.6°F, versus the +5°F needed to build a thermal), and the coastal station ensemble shows 0% southerly flow. There is no thermal component tonight — wind direction and magnitude both track the synoptic gradient (internally, B-moderate).

RYC reads NNE at 11.1 kt instantaneous / 13.8 kt 10-min average, gusting to 25.6 kt — a notably gusty ratio (~1.9x sustained) that lines up with the active Wind Advisory for the region (north wind near 20 mph, gusts to 32 mph, in effect since 2:48 PM today through Sunday morning). The authoritative station mean sits right at 15.0 kt, on the strong edge of the moderate band.

HRRR's f01–f05 hourly forecast (out to 8 PM) holds essentially steady at 14–15 kt, backing slightly from N to NNE (8°→15°), which agrees well with RYC's current direction (026°) and the ensemble median (013°) — no meaningful model/obs divergence to flag. The model's usable horizon runs out at 8 PM; the 9–10 PM hours are extrapolated from that steady trend, carrying the same speed and gust ratio forward.

Per gradient rules, this holds through sunset (6:46 PM) and beyond since it isn't solar-driven — don't expect any evening collapse.

At N–NNE, the flow sits right on the boundary between the cove geography table's cleanest "NE" lane and the puffier, shiftier "N–NW" lane — and RYC's gust ratio (near 2x sustained) says the puffy, shifty character is winning tonight. Expect the best average pressure mid-cove, away from the immediate lee of the NW shore, with real gust/lull swings closer to the shorelines.

Shift character should stay steady and persistent (synoptic gradient, no thermal oscillation) rather than any tactical oscillating pattern — no frontal signal in the pressure trend. Treat the big swings tonight as gust-driven, not directional shifts.

data_caveats: HRRR forecast only extends through 8:00 PM (f01–f05); f06–f12 fetch/parse failed, so the 9–10 PM wind values are extrapolated from the established trend, not directly modeled.
Buoy 44040 (WLIS_MET) offline — UConn ERDDAP endpoint returned 404.
Several surface stations (KBDR, KHPN, KHVN, KISP, KFOK, KIJD) have missing wind sensors/anemometers and were excluded from the ensemble as outliers.
A Coastal Flood Warning in the NWS alerts feed has an invalid time window (expires before its own onset) — treated as stale and excluded from the risk call.
A regional Wind Advisory is active now through Sunday 6 AM (gusts to 32 mph) — a wind hazard, not a thunderstorm hazard, but it drives the elevated storm.risk_level and the gusty wind-side forecast.
